sections.heading: C — Crash Procedures, Safety Responsibility Law and Motor Vehicle Insurance
sections.markdown:
## C — Crash Procedures, Safety Responsibility Law and Motor Vehicle Insurance

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
A traffic crash that causes any personal injury, a death, or property damage of three thousand dollars or more must be reported to the police immediately by the quickest means of communication [A01].
Why it matters: the three-thousand-dollar damage threshold is the number to remember.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
If you are in a crash, stop immediately, move your vehicle off the traveled part of the road if possible, and never leave the scene without identifying yourself and rendering assistance [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
Help the injured by calling the nearest police agency and asking for an ambulance if needed, then act promptly but carefully without moving injured people unnecessarily, because unskilled handling can turn minor injuries into serious ones [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
Keep an injured person warm until skilled help arrives, try to stop severe bleeding with direct pressure, and protect the victim from oncoming traffic [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
Have someone warn approaching cars to prevent further damage, and keep a flashlight and flares in your vehicle for such emergencies [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A01
At a crash a driver must give name, address and vehicle registration information, and on request show a driver's license, to anyone injured and to the driver, occupant or attendant of any vehicle or other property that was damaged [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A01
If you strike an unattended vehicle you must stop and find the owner or leave a written notice with your name, address and the circumstances, and if you damage other property along the highway you must notify its owner [A01].
Why it matters: the written-notice duty applies even when no one is around.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A02
The motor vehicle safety responsibility law affects every driver involved in a crash that causes death, injury or property damage over three thousand dollars, and every person convicted in court of certain vehicle offenses [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A02
After such a crash you must report it to the police department and your insurance company and file evidence of insurance on form SR twenty-one [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A02
After conviction of certain vehicle offenses you must file and maintain proof of financial responsibility for three years from the conviction date and file evidence of insurance on form SR twenty-two [A02].
Why it matters: SR twenty-one follows a crash, SR twenty-two follows a conviction, and the conviction filing lasts three years.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A02
The penalty for failing to comply with the safety responsibility law is suspension of the driver's license [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A03
Every owner of a car, bus or truck must carry motor vehicle insurance in order to register or operate the vehicle in Hawaii [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A03
The basic mandatory benefits include up to ten thousand dollars per person for medical and rehabilitative expenses [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A03
Mandatory liability coverage is twenty thousand dollars per person with an aggregate of forty thousand dollars per accident for bodily injury, plus ten thousand dollars per accident for property damage, and damage to your own car is not covered without additional coverage [A03].
Why it matters: the twenty, forty and ten thousand figures are the classic minimum-coverage question.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A03
You can sue or be sued for property damage at any time, but for bodily injury only when medical bills exceed five thousand dollars, when the injury causes loss of use of a body part or function or permanent and serious disfigurement, or when the injury results in death [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A03
Each violation of the motor vehicle insurance law is a separate offense punishable by a fine of up to five thousand dollars or thirty days in jail, suspension of the driver's license, forfeiture of the vehicle registration certificate, or any combination of these [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0054]

Misconceptions: basic insurance does not cover damage to your own car; the crash report threshold is three thousand dollars of property damage, while the bodily-injury lawsuit threshold is five thousand dollars of medical bills; SR twenty-one is the crash filing and SR twenty-two is the conviction filing kept for three years; you must leave a written notice after hitting an unattended vehicle even if no one saw it; injured people should not be moved unnecessarily.

Mnemonics: Three thousand to report, five thousand in medical bills to sue; twenty, forty and ten thousand are the liability minimums and ten thousand is the medical benefit; twenty-one after a crash, twenty-two after a conviction, for three years.

Glossary: safety responsibility law (the law requiring proof of financial responsibility after crashes and convictions); SR twenty-one (the evidence of insurance form filed after a crash); SR twenty-two (the evidence of insurance form filed after a conviction); aggregate limit (the total payable per accident regardless of how many people are injured); forfeiture of registration (loss of the vehicle's registration certificate as a penalty).

Dynamic facts: the dollar thresholds, coverage minimums and penalties are statutory amounts that the legislature can change between printings, so they are stated exactly as this edition prints them and should be rechecked at each new edition.

corpus_stability.reason: The Hawaii Driver's Manual is a periodically reprinted reference (imprint HMG 5/2023, copyright line through 2023); the what to do at a crash, the reporting threshold, the safety responsibility law and its filings, mandatory insurance coverages, when you can sue for injury, and the insurance law penalties rules on pages 52–54 are statutory and procedural content that changes less than once a year, so no BlockedProbe.
